steps.say: To infer means to work something out from clues. Writers often show feelings instead of naming them.
Ask what the character does, says or notices. Then think what that would mean in real life.
steps.show: knuckles turned white → holding very tightly → nervous

steps.say: Always find evidence. Point to the words in the text that support your answer.
steps.show: Evidence: so tightly that his knuckles turned white

steps.say: For a new word, read the sentences around it and look for clues.
steps.show: tangled up ... cut it free → caught and twisted

steps.say: Some phrases are not meant to be taken literally.
steps.show: My legs were burning = my legs were very tired

check.prompt:
Ana slammed the door and stomped up the stairs.
How does Ana feel?

options.why: Slamming and stomping are not calm actions.
A sleepy person would move slowly and quietly.
Nothing here shows that she is proud.

hints: How do people shut doors when they are upset?
check.explanation: Slamming the door and stomping up the stairs are clues that Ana is cross.

check.prompt:
The soup was so hot that steam curled up from the bowl. Dad blew on his spoon.
Why did Dad blow on his spoon?

options.why: Blowing on a spoon does not make music.
The spoon has hot soup on it.

options.text: to show the soup was cold
options.why: The text says the soup was very hot.

hints: What do you know about the soup?
What do people do when food is too hot to eat?
Link the steam to what Dad does next.
check.explanation: The soup was very hot, so Dad blew on his spoon to cool it before eating.
